analysis: The 6am tape adds two industrial beats against the tech-weakness narrative: Northrop Grumman (EPS $7.89 vs $7.19 est, raised FY2026 adj-EPS to $29.35-29.75, record $109.6B backlog, first 2027 outlook with sales +5-7% and FCF $3.3-3.5B, +1.8% premarket) and GE Aerospace (adj. EPS $2.25 vs $2.01 est, revenue $14.12B vs $12.88B est, raised FY2026 adj-EPS to $8.00-8.10, orders +49%, premarket mixed) both beat and raised, though both stocks carry defense-rate overhangs into the open. The AI-debt selloff remains the dominant tape pressure: CoreWeave's co-founders reportedly sold $3.3B of stock since the March 2025 IPO (single-source, fragile), the stock hit a 52-week low, memory names are weak again on Chinese competition (SanDisk -3% premarket, SK Hynix -4.7% premarket as Kospi fell 3.9% overnight), and Elice Group's debut flopped ~30% below IPO price. Apple's UK CMA NFC proposal (Reuters-confirmed, consultation to Nov 17) adds regulatory overhang to AAPL (-1% premarket). Oil keeps its macro role: WTI rebounded to +2.5% at $106.20 after Brent touched $111.05, the 10Y slipped to 5.11% (down from 5.14%), and the Fed-hold consensus is unchanged. Versus the 5am brief: the story moved from 'GM beat-and-down + oil five-month high' to 'industrials beat-and-raise vs AI names under pressure, futures pointing to a lower open'.

headlines.headline: Northrop Grumman beat Q3: diluted EPS $7.89 vs $7.19 consensus on $11.1B sales (+7%), raised FY2026 MTM-adjusted EPS guidance to $29.35-29.75 (from $28.60-29.10), booked $16.4B in awards, backlog hit a record $109.6B, and gave a first 2027 outlook: sales growth of 5-7% and free cash flow of $3.3-3.5B. Shares rose ~1.8% premarket to just under $520.
headlines.why_it_matters: Beat-and-raise on record backlog plus a 2027 growth outlook — positive earnings read for the name, though the stock is still down 10% YTD on defense-sector overhangs.

headlines.headline: GE Aerospace beat Q3: adjusted EPS $2.25 vs $2.01 consensus, revenue $14.12B (+16%) vs $12.88B estimate, orders up 49% to $19.0B; raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $8.00-8.10 (from $7.65-7.85) and adjusted revenue growth to 19-20%. Premarket trading was mixed after a $311.28 Monday close.
headlines.why_it_matters: Strong commercial-engine demand (services +21%) keeps the aerospace upcycle intact — positive industrial signal offsetting tech weakness.

headlines.headline: The UK's Competition and Markets Authority on Tuesday proposed forcing Apple to lower access fees and open its iPhone NFC/contactless technology to rival wallets under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act; consultation runs to November 17. Apple fell ~1% premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: Another regulatory overhang on Apple's services moat in a market where contactless is 39% of all UK payments — proposal stage only, so the tape impact is headline-driven.

headlines.headline: Reports say CoreWeave's three co-founders have sold $3.3B of stock since the March 2025 IPO, including $2.4B in 2026; the stock traded down ~3-4% premarket and sits at 52-week lows after last week's 25% slide on AI-debt fears.
headlines.why_it_matters: Insider-selling reports feed the AI-debt-confidence narrative that has been pressing tech — single-source, unconfirmed by the company; treat as fragile.

headlines.headline: Futures point to a lower open (Investopedia, ~30 min ago): Nasdaq futures -0.8%, S&P 500 futures -0.3%, Dow futures fractionally lower. WTI crude is back up +2.5% at $106.20 after trading above $110 earlier; Brent near five-month highs. Gold -0.6% at $4,135/oz, bitcoin $81,400, 10Y Treasury at 5.11% (down from 5.14% Monday).
headlines.why_it_matters: The combination of tech-weakness and the oil rebound points to a risk-off open — negative setup for the regular session.

headlines.headline: Carried forward: DHS ordered federal civilian agencies to remove DeepSeek AI models/products from IT systems and barred future purchases (notice published Monday, appears in the Federal Register Tuesday), citing potential transfer of sensitive data to China; businesses and individuals are not affected.
headlines.why_it_matters: Continued US-China AI decoupling policy — neutral for equities near-term, relevant context for AI trade sentiment.

headlines.headline: Carried forward: GM's Q3 core profit rose 22% to $4.1B (adj. EPS $3.70 vs $3.63 consensus) but shares fell premarket after it narrowed 2026 adj. EPS guidance to $12.75-13.75, midpoint below the $13.41 consensus; board authorized a $20B buyback and pegged commodity inflation at ~$2B.
headlines.why_it_matters: Beat-and-down on guidance keeps tariff/cost pressure on the tape ahead of the tech earnings block.
